description: A server-side application exposing data through HTTP endpoints. Examples: task manager API, user authentication system, data pipeline, portfolio backend, sports stats tracker.

phases.core_concept: REST semantics — resources, verbs, and status codes, and why professionals design the API surface for [PROJECT_PURPOSE] before writing any code
ai_appropriate_tasks: Generate an OpenAPI-style outline from your finished resource list
Generate example request/response payloads for each planned endpoint
human_required_tasks: List the resources in [PROJECT_PURPOSE] and the operations each one supports
Decide the URL structure and HTTP method for every endpoint
Define what 401, 403, and 404 each mean in your API and when each one is returned
explanation_gate_targets: Why these resources and operations model [PROJECT_PURPOSE], and what you deliberately left out
The difference between 401, 403, and 404 in your API, with a concrete endpoint example of each
The full lifecycle of one request through your planned API, from arrival to response
phases.unlock_condition: 3-turn gate passed with no unresolved follow-ups
phases.functional_unlock: Pre-configured FastAPI skeleton matching your resource list — skip project scaffolding at the start of Phase 2

phases.core_concept: FastAPI structure — routers, Pydantic validation, startup config, and the service layer where all database and external calls live
ai_appropriate_tasks: Generate router boilerplate from your endpoint list
Generate Pydantic models from your payload examples
human_required_tasks: Structure the app — models, services, routers, config — and decide what lives where and why
Write the config module that validates every environment variable at startup
Wire the first endpoint end to end and test it in the auto-generated /docs
explanation_gate_targets: Why service logic is separated from route handlers in your project, with an example from your code
What Pydantic rejects automatically on your endpoints, and what you still have to check yourself
How your config module behaves if an environment variable is missing, and why it fails at startup
phases.unlock_condition: 3-turn gate passed with no unresolved follow-ups
phases.functional_unlock: Pre-configured logging and error-handler middleware — skip that setup in Phase 6

phases.core_concept: Schema design with security first — Row Level Security and ownership policies before any query code is written
ai_appropriate_tasks: Generate the SQL for your schema after tables and ownership columns are decided
human_required_tasks: Enable RLS on this table and write an ownership policy before continuing. Do not proceed until this is done.
Design the tables with a user_id ownership column and the relationships [PROJECT_PURPOSE] needs
Decide where the anon key and the service-role key are each used. NOTE: The service-role key bypasses RLS — it exists only in backend environment variables, never in any client or committed file.
explanation_gate_targets: What your RLS policy actually enforces, and why 'user is logged in' is not sufficient — ownership must be verified
What happens if the ownership check were removed from your main table — what anyone with your anon key could do
Why the service-role key can never appear in client code, and where yours actually lives
Why you modeled the relationships this way for [PROJECT_PURPOSE]
phases.unlock_condition: 3-turn gate passed with no unresolved follow-ups
phases.functional_unlock: Based on how you explained your schema, you've unlocked the advanced query builder — pre-written complex queries for your specific schema

phases.core_concept: Server-side auth — JWT verification middleware, and ownership checks on every route that touches user data
ai_appropriate_tasks: Generate the JWT decoding boilerplate once the verification design is decided
Generate scripts that create test users
human_required_tasks: Write the auth verification middleware and attach it to every route that touches user data. NOTE: Hiding this in the UI does not protect it. This check must happen here, in the backend, on every request.
Decide the 401 versus 403/404 behavior for each protected endpoint
Run the two-account test: create Users A and B; with B's token, request A's resource ID. You must get 403 or 404, not data. Do not proceed until this passes.
explanation_gate_targets: What happens if the auth middleware is removed from one route — who can then do what in your API
Why hiding endpoints from documentation or a UI does not protect them
How your middleware gets from the Authorization header to a trusted user identity, step by step
What your two-account test proved, exactly, and what it did not prove
phases.unlock_condition: 3-turn gate passed with no unresolved follow-ups
phases.functional_unlock: Pre-configured auth test suite for your endpoints — skip writing the protected-route tests manually in Phase 6

phases.core_concept: Business logic on protected resources — validation at the boundary, parameterized queries, and consistent error shapes
ai_appropriate_tasks: Generate the repetitive CRUD handlers after the first one is written and fully understood
Generate validation test cases from your rules
human_required_tasks: Write the first full CRUD path yourself: validate input, check ownership, query with parameters, shape the response
Validate every user input that reaches the database and use parameterized queries — never string concatenation
Define the error response shape used consistently across the whole API
explanation_gate_targets: What breaks if input validation is removed from your create endpoint — demonstrate what a malicious payload could do
Why parameterized queries stop injection where string concatenation does not, using your own query code
Where ownership is checked in your update path, and what happens without it
Why your error responses share one shape, and what leaks if they don't
phases.unlock_condition: 3-turn gate passed with no unresolved follow-ups
phases.functional_unlock: Pre-built pagination and filtering module for your list endpoints — skip the manual offset/limit work

phases.core_concept: Making the API trustworthy — exception handling, a pytest suite that proves auth and ownership, and docs that expose nothing internal
ai_appropriate_tasks: Generate additional test cases patterned on your happy-path tests
Generate endpoint descriptions for the OpenAPI docs
human_required_tasks: Write the pytest suite covering: no token → 401, wrong user → 403/404, invalid payload → 422
Decide how unexpected exceptions are caught and exactly what the client sees instead of a stack trace
Review the auto-generated /docs and confirm nothing internal (fields, keys, admin routes) is exposed
explanation_gate_targets: Which failure cases your test suite actually proves, and which it doesn't
What the client sees when your database call throws, and why not a stack trace
How you'd know if a future change silently broke an ownership check
phases.unlock_condition: 3-turn gate passed with no unresolved follow-ups
phases.functional_unlock: Pre-configured CI workflow that runs your test suite on every push — skip the pipeline setup

phases.core_concept: Verification, not learning — confirming against your actual running API that every security constraint you built is really enforced before you ship
ai_appropriate_tasks: Generate a search script for secret patterns (api_key, secret, sk_live, token, password) across the codebase
human_required_tasks: Search the entire codebase for api_key, secret, sk_live, token, password. Confirm none appear in any frontend file or any file committed to the public repo.
Open browser DevTools Network tab. Make requests in the app. Confirm no secrets appear in any request or response payload.
Confirm all external API calls with secrets are made from backend functions, not frontend code.
Open Supabase Authentication → Policies. Confirm RLS is enabled on every table. Confirm every policy checks ownership, not just login status.
Attempt to access a protected route directly via URL or curl without being logged in. Confirm it returns 401, not data.
Attempt to access another user's data by manipulating a resource ID in a request. Confirm it returns 403 or 404, not the other user's data.
Confirm every user input that reaches the database uses parameterized queries, not string concatenation.
Confirm every user input that gets rendered in the UI is sanitized or escaped before rendering.
Run the app URL with /api, /admin, /dashboard, and other common paths appended. Document what responds and confirm nothing sensitive is exposed unintentionally.
explanation_gate_targets: Walk me through one item on this checklist. Tell me what you checked, what you found, and what you did or confirmed as a result.
Which checklist item surprised you or failed on first check in your API, and what you changed
Which single checklist item would be most damaging to skip for [PROJECT_PURPOSE], and what a stranger could do if you had skipped it
phases.unlock_condition: 3-turn gate passed with no unresolved follow-ups
phases.functional_unlock: Your gate scores across this project qualify you for the system design review — a full written architectural critique of your codebase you can reference in interviews
